punchline: Nash took his strange ideas seriously because they arrived like his mathematics.
thirty_sec: In spring 1959, Harvard mathematician George Mackey visited John Nash in hospital and asked how a man devoted to reason could believe aliens were recruiting him. According to Sylvia Nasar, Nash answered that those ideas had come to him the way his mathematical ideas did, so he took them seriously.
question: Which belief of yours feels completely obvious, and what outside check has it passed?
key_contrast: How certain an idea feels says nothing about whether it is true.
